auftrag.title: [Auftrag] Switch the Claude account behind a Claude setup without logging out

label: Criteria Review
bodySnapshot:
### Repository

~/shared/fastnd/t3code

### Blocked by

_No response_

### Settings

_No response_

### Behavioural requirements

- T3 can remember the Claude account currently logged in on one of its Claude setups, under a name the user chooses. Several accounts can be remembered per machine.
- The user can see which accounts T3 remembers and which one is active on each Claude setup.
- The user can make T3 forget an account. Forgetting the active account does not log that setup out.
- The user can switch a Claude setup to another remembered account. Afterwards every thread that uses this setup works with the new account, and no thread loses its history.
- Turns that are running on that setup when the switch starts are stopped cleanly; their threads can be continued afterwards on the new account.
- Before switching away, T3 saves the latest login of the outgoing account, so switching back later works without logging in again.
- A switch changes only which account is logged in. Everything else that belongs to the setup (settings, history, other logins) stays exactly as it was.
- A switch either completes or leaves the setup exactly as before. There is never a half-switched state.
- If Claude programs outside T3 are using the same setup, T3 refuses the switch and says why.
- If the saved login of the target account no longer works, the user is told that this account needs a fresh login.
- Remembered logins are stored as securely as T3's other secrets and never appear in logs, threads or the UI.
- This Auftrag delivers these functions in the backend only and makes sure they work there. A separate frontend Auftrag will follow and make them accessible to the user in T3's screens. How they are triggered from the frontend is not part of this Auftrag.
- Only Linux is supported; on other systems these actions say they are unavailable.

### Purpose

- Subscription usage limits stop work mid-task. Switching accounts keeps threads going without a logout/login round trip and without losing context.
- One setup is shared by many threads; switching per thread would leave them disagreeing about who is logged in.
- Logins renew themselves over time, and an outdated copy locks the account out. That is why the outgoing login is saved at the moment of switching.
- The setup also holds history and other logins the user depends on; a switch must never cost them.
- Programs outside T3 would overwrite the switch or be broken by it; refusing is safer than guessing.
- Splitting backend and frontend keeps each Auftrag small. The frontend Auftrag needs time for mocks, and it can build on functions that are already proven to work.
- This is a personal build; Linux is the only platform in use, so other systems are out of scope.

### Mocks

None. This Auftrag adds no screens; a follow-up frontend Auftrag will come with mocks.

### No technical details

- [X] This Auftrag names no files, libraries, tables or architecture. That is the Gremium's job.

### Acceptance criteria

<details>
<summary>31 scenarios</summary>

```gherkin
Scenario AK-1: Remember the account logged in on a setup under a chosen name
  Given a Claude setup on which the account "alice@example.com" is logged in
  And T3 remembers no accounts yet
  When T3 is asked to remember this setup's account under the name "Work"
  Then T3 remembers one account named "Work" for "alice@example.com"
Serves: R1

Scenario AK-2: Several accounts can be remembered on one machine
  Given T3 remembers the account "alice@example.com" under the name "Work"
  And a second Claude setup on which "bob@example.com" is logged in
  When T3 is asked to remember the second setup's account under the name "Private"
  Then T3 remembers both "Work" and "Private"
Serves: R1

Scenario AK-3: Remembering is refused when no account is logged in
  Given a Claude setup on which no account is logged in
  When T3 is asked to remember this setup's account under the name "Work"
  Then the request is refused with the reason that no account is logged in on this setup
  And T3 remembers no new account
Serves: R1

Scenario AK-4: Remembering under a name already in use is refused
  Given T3 remembers "alice@example.com" under the name "Work"
  And a Claude setup on which "bob@example.com" is logged in
  When T3 is asked to remember this setup's account under the name "Work"
  Then the request is refused with the reason that the name "Work" is already in use
  And "Work" still stands for "alice@example.com"
Serves: R1

Scenario AK-5: List shows remembered accounts and the active account per setup
  Given T3 remembers "Work" for "alice@example.com" and "Private" for "bob@example.com"
  And setup one has "alice@example.com" logged in and setup two has "bob@example.com" logged in
  When T3 is asked which accounts it remembers
  Then the answer names "Work" and "Private"
  And it shows "Work" as active on setup one and "Private" as active on setup two
Serves: R2

Scenario AK-6: List shows an active account that is not remembered
  Given a Claude setup on which "carol@example.com" is logged in
  And T3 does not remember "carol@example.com"
  When T3 is asked which accounts it remembers
  Then the answer shows "carol@example.com" as active on that setup
  And it marks that account as not remembered
Serves: R2

Scenario AK-7: List with nothing remembered
  Given T3 remembers no accounts
  When T3 is asked which accounts it remembers
  Then the answer contains no remembered accounts
  And it still shows which account is active on each Claude setup
Serves: R2

Scenario AK-8: Forget an account that is not active
  Given T3 remembers "Work" and "Private"
  And no Claude setup has the "Private" account active
  When T3 is asked to forget "Private"
  Then T3 remembers only "Work"
Serves: R3

Scenario AK-9: Forgetting the active account keeps the setup logged in
  Given a Claude setup with "alice@example.com" logged in, remembered as "Work"
  When T3 is asked to forget "Work"
  Then T3 no longer remembers "Work"
  And the setup is still logged in as "alice@example.com"
  And a new turn in a thread on that setup runs as "alice@example.com"
Serves: R3

Scenario AK-10: After a switch, every thread on the setup works with the new account
  Given a Claude setup with "Work" active and "Private" remembered
  And two idle threads in different projects that use this setup
  When T3 is asked to switch the setup to "Private"
  Then the setup shows "Private" as active
  And a new turn in each of the two threads runs as the "Private" account
Serves: R4

Scenario AK-11: A switch keeps every thread's history
  Given a Claude setup with "Work" active and "Private" remembered
  And a thread on this setup with earlier messages and turns
  When T3 is asked to switch the setup to "Private"
  Then the thread still shows all of its earlier messages and turns
  And a new turn in that thread continues the same conversation
Serves: R4

Scenario AK-12: A switch does not touch threads on another setup
  Given setup one with "Work" active and "Private" remembered
  And setup two with "bob@example.com" active
  And an idle thread on setup two
  When T3 is asked to switch setup one to "Private"
  Then setup two still shows "bob@example.com" as active
  And a new turn in the thread on setup two runs as "bob@example.com"
Serves: R4

Scenario AK-13: A running turn on the setup is stopped cleanly by a switch
  Given a Claude setup with "Work" active and "Private" remembered
  And a thread on this setup with a turn still running
  When T3 is asked to switch the setup to "Private"
  Then the running turn ends as stopped, not as failed
  And the thread is no longer shown as working
Serves: R5

Scenario AK-14: A thread stopped by a switch continues on the new account
  Given a thread whose running turn was stopped by a switch of its setup to "Private"
  When the user sends a new message in that thread
  Then the new turn runs as the "Private" account
  And it continues the same conversation
Serves: R5

Scenario AK-15: Running turns on another setup are not stopped
  Given setup one with "Work" active and "Private" remembered
  And a thread on setup two with a turn still running
  When T3 is asked to switch setup one to "Private"
  Then the turn on setup two keeps running
Serves: R5

Scenario AK-16: Switching back works with the login renewed in the meantime
  Given a Claude setup with "Work" active and "Private" remembered
  And the "Work" login on the setup renewed itself after "Work" was remembered
  And the setup was then switched to "Private"
  When T3 is asked to switch the setup back to "Work"
  Then the setup shows "Work" as active
  And a new turn on that setup runs as "Work" without a fresh login
Serves: R6

Scenario AK-17: Switching away from an account T3 does not remember is refused
  Given a Claude setup on which "carol@example.com" is logged in but not remembered
  And "Private" is remembered
  When T3 is asked to switch the setup to "Private"
  Then the switch is refused with the reason that the current account must be remembered first
  And the setup is still logged in as "carol@example.com"
Serves: R6

Scenario AK-18: A switch leaves the rest of the setup unchanged
  Given a Claude setup with "Work" active and "Private" remembered
  And the setup holds its own settings, conversation history and logins for other services
  When T3 is asked to switch the setup to "Private"
  Then the settings, conversation history and other logins are exactly as they were before
  And only the logged-in Claude account has changed
Serves: R7

Scenario AK-19: A switch that fails partway leaves the setup as before
  Given a Claude setup with "Work" active and "Private" remembered
  And the switch will be interrupted by a failure after it has started changing the setup
  When T3 is asked to switch the setup to "Private"
  Then the switch reports that it failed
  And the setup is logged in as "Work" exactly as before
  And a new turn on that setup runs as "Work"
Serves: R8

Scenario AK-20: A switch is refused while Claude programs outside T3 use the setup
  Given a Claude setup with "Work" active and "Private" remembered
  And a Claude program started outside T3 is using the same setup
  When T3 is asked to switch the setup to "Private"
  Then the switch is refused with the reason that Claude programs outside T3 are using this setup
  And the setup is still logged in as "Work"
Serves: R9

Scenario AK-21: A refused switch leaves running T3 turns alone
  Given a Claude setup with "Work" active and "Private" remembered
  And a Claude program started outside T3 is using the same setup
  And a thread on this setup with a turn still running in T3
  When T3 is asked to switch the setup to "Private"
  Then the switch is refused
  And the running turn keeps running
Serves: R9

Scenario AK-22: Switching to an account whose saved login no longer works
  Given a Claude setup with "Work" active
  And "Private" is remembered but its saved login no longer works
  When T3 is asked to switch the setup to "Private"
  Then the answer says that "Private" needs a fresh login
  And the setup is still logged in as "Work"
Serves: R10

Scenario AK-23: Remembered logins are kept in T3's protected secret storage
  Given a Claude setup with "alice@example.com" logged in
  When T3 is asked to remember this setup's account under the name "Work"
  Then the saved login is kept with the same protection as T3's other secrets
  And it cannot be found in plain form anywhere else in T3's own data
Serves: R11

Scenario AK-24: The account list never reveals a login
  Given T3 remembers "Work" and "Private"
  When T3 is asked which accounts it remembers
  Then the answer contains names, account identities and which one is active
  And it contains no part of any saved login
Serves: R11

Scenario AK-25: Logs and threads never reveal a login
  Given T3 remembers "Work" and "Private" on a Claude setup with threads
  When T3 is asked to switch the setup from "Work" to "Private"
  Then T3's logs contain no part of either login
  And no thread contains any part of either login
Serves: R11

Scenario AK-26: A switch works in the backend without any screen
  Given a T3 server on Linux with no account screens in any client
  And a Claude setup with "Work" active and "Private" remembered
  When the switch to "Private" is requested directly from the server, without a client
  Then the switch completes and reports "Private" as active
Serves: R12

Scenario AK-27: Remembering is unavailable outside Linux
  Given a T3 server running on a system other than Linux
  When T3 is asked to remember a setup's account
  Then the answer says the action is unavailable on this system
  And nothing is remembered
Serves: R13

Scenario AK-28: Listing is unavailable outside Linux
  Given a T3 server running on a system other than Linux
  When T3 is asked which accounts it remembers
  Then the answer says the action is unavailable on this system
Serves: R13

Scenario AK-29: Forgetting is unavailable outside Linux
  Given a T3 server running on a system other than Linux
  When T3 is asked to forget a remembered account
  Then the answer says the action is unavailable on this system
Serves: R13

Scenario AK-30: Switching is unavailable outside Linux
  Given a T3 server running on a system other than Linux with a Claude setup that has "Work" active
  When T3 is asked to switch the setup to another account
  Then the answer says the action is unavailable on this system
  And the setup is still logged in as "Work"
Serves: R13

Scenario AK-31: A switch refused for an unremembered account leaves running turns alone
  Given a Claude setup on which "carol@example.com" is logged in but not remembered
  And "Private" is remembered
  And a thread on this setup with a turn still running
  When T3 is asked to switch the setup to "Private"
  Then the switch is refused
  And the running turn keeps running
Serves: R6
```

</details>
